question: State two experimental observations of the photoelectric effect which cannot be explained on the basis of wave theory of light.

options.A: Photoelectric current increases with intensity, and the energy of photoelectrons increases with intensity.
options.B: Photoelectric emission occurs for all frequencies if the light intensity is high enough, and emission is delayed at high frequency.
options.C: Photoelectrons are emitted only after a measurable time lag, and no threshold frequency exists.
options.D: For a given metal, emission occurs only above a threshold frequency, and photoelectrons are emitted almost instantaneously when suitable radiation falls on the surface. Wave theory cannot explain these observations.
